COVID-19, caused by the novel coronavirus SARS-CoV-2, spreads through respiratory droplets when an infected person coughs, sneezes, or talks. The rapid spread of COVID-19 across regions with and without 5G coverage further undermines the theory that 5G is responsible for the virus [1]. Countries with advanced 5G infrastructure experienced the same patterns of viral transmission as those without, and health officials in countries where 5G was already deployed reported cases of COVID-19 before the networks were widely used [1]. Conspiracy theories linking 5G to COVID-19 can have serious consequences for public health, leading to distrust in legitimate health advice and avoidance of necessary medical care [0]. Health organizations worldwide, including the WHO, have repeatedly stated that there is no link between 5G and COVID-19 [1]. It is crucial to rely on facts and trusted sources of information, such as health organizations, when addressing public health issues [1]. The fight against COVID-19 requires unity, cooperation, and reliance on science, not unfounded fears and misinformation [1].
